### **Topics Taught by Siddharth**

Siddharth's instruction on caching, embeddings, and context window limits emphasizes foundational understanding and practical application within LLM-based systems, specifically focusing on efficiency, cost optimization, and effective prompt engineering.

*   **Caching Fundamentals and Implementation**: Siddharth extensively taught the concept of caching, defining it as a mechanism to avoid redundant computations and optimize resource usage [2026-07-30, Page 1 — Siddharth Saminathan]. He illustrated this with real-world examples, such as applications remaining open on a computer, to explain the core principle of not loading data "from scratch again" [2026-07-30, Page 1 — Siddharth Saminathan]. He specifically highlighted its critical role in reducing **embedding costs at scale**, stating, "Caching, embeddings, how to, you know, save on embedding costs at scale. Those will be, these buttons will haunt you forever. As long as you are an AI engineer, in every interview they will ask you" [2026-07-22, Page 3-4 — Siddharth Saminathan]. He also stressed that caching is for future users and concurrent usage, ensuring costs come down as user numbers grow [2026-07-22, Page 3 — Siddharth Saminathan]. He prompted trainees to recall *how* to implement caching, noting different types like embedding caching, LLM caching, and prompt caching [2026-07-30, Page 1 — Siddharth Saminathan].

*   **Embeddings and Cost Optimization**: Directly linked to caching, Siddharth taught the significance of efficiently managing embeddings. He demonstrated how re-embedding data repeatedly is wasteful [2026-07-22, Page 3-4 — Siddharth Saminathan]. He posed a scenario to Dakshinya where, with a large user base (1 million to 1.5 million users), the goal was to reduce embedding costs by 70%, explicitly asking for the "first step in reducing the cost of embeddings" [2026-07-22, Page 13-14 — Siddharth Saminathan]. He guided her to identify caching as the primary solution, followed by "data of noise filter" (signal-to-noise ratio) [2026-07-22, Page 13-14 — Siddharth Saminathan]. He also asked Himaya why he initially brought up caching, which was to avoid loading data "again and again" and to "load the data second in meeting" [2026-07-22, Page 1-2 — Siddharth Saminathan]. He specifically asked Himaya to cache embeddings in vector form locally [2026-07-22, Page 1-2 — Siddharth Saminathan]. For Dakshinya, he mentioned the need to "re-embed everything" if user scoping metadata was not included, emphasizing the architectural implications of embedding design [2026-07-28, Page 13-14 — Siddharth Saminathan].

*   **Context Window Limits and Token Management**: While not as explicitly detailed as caching and embeddings, Siddharth touched upon context window limits implicitly through discussions on token management and passing data to LLMs. When Ganesh proposed putting Excel data into a database for LLM access, Siddharth questioned the approach, noting Ganesh's own concern that passing "JSON of thousands and all to directly to LLM will it be like it will be context heavy right and the tokens and all will be Very much" [2026-07-14, Page 7-9 — Siddharth Saminathan]. This directly addresses the practical implications of large inputs on an LLM's context window and associated token costs. He later advised trainees to "take a look at this file, so that you guys understand what is context window and problem for the last time" [2026-07-28, Page 17 — Siddharth Saminathan], indicating a direct teaching moment on this topic. His emphasis on semantic chunking and prompt building in the RAG system design also implicitly relates to managing context effectively within LLM limits [2026-08-17, Page 4-5 — Siddharth Saminathan].
